content.rationale: S5-bracket fixes the protocol — the op head read before the operation runs and again after, the run itself untouched — S5-lifecycle which invocations feed it, G-capture and G-footprint (xwnylypn) that the window's entries attributed to the invoking workspace are what a bracket keeps, and S5-observation (urqytyqn) that the bracket settles the working copy once before its window and again after the run returns and that the reads leave it alone, so the plain capture closes its window on the settle of the run's own writes while a recording keeps the one settle its journal entry is taken inside; M-layout places the module flat at src/markers_capture.rs. A recording additionally snapshots the target's owned paths before and after the run and stores one journal entry (S5-journal-capture, wxtzltkt) through M-journal (zutqsqtu), so the marker's recording entry names that entry. It crosses M-jj's runner and reads the head, the window and the invoking workspace through M-jj-oplog, appends through M-markers-append, and names the store and the carried reasons through M-store and M-markers-persist. One transition, closing on the settle of the run's own write: settle the working copy (`jj util snapshot`) before the pre-read, read the live op head, run the given operation untouched, settle the working copy again after the run returns and before the closing read, read the head again, keep the window's entries that are the invoking workspace's own — so another workspace's entries that share the window are not the operation's, a snapshot of edits that predate the invocation is outside the window rather than in it, and the write the run itself left on a tracked path is snapshotted inside the operation's own window as one of its entries, leaving nothing for a later jj call to snapshot as an entry of its own. The closing settle is the bracket's own leg, taken after the run returns rather than inside it, so the run stays untouched and both head reads still observe the op log without snapshotting. A failed settle or read aborts before the run, so nothing is bracketed that never opened; the run's own outcome passes through unexamined, so which invocation brackets stays the caller's call and every failure is carried, never rendered. The run answers the target it named (S5-record-named, wotmvzyt); one that answers none closes its bracket and records nothing — no entries are kept and no marker is appended — and one whose window kept no entries records nothing too, so a no-op buys no un-undoable step and the marker file is left as it stood; a run that names a target and kept work records even when it fails, because that work landed before the refusal.
